title: Identify SLA Breaches Using DATEDIFF
description:
For each support ticket calculate the number of days to resolve it and flag whether it breached the assigned SLA (days_to_resolve > sla_days).

**Table: support_tickets** — `id`, `customer_id`, `created_date`, `resolved_date`, `sla_days`

Output columns: `id`, `customer_id`, `days_to_resolve`, `sla_days`, `sla_status`. Order by `id`.
solution_sql: SELECT id, customer_id, DATEDIFF('day', created_date, resolved_date) AS days_to_resolve, sla_days, CASE WHEN DATEDIFF('day', created_date, resolved_date) > sla_days THEN 'SLA Breach' ELSE 'On Time' END AS sla_status FROM support_tickets ORDER BY id

test_cases.description: 8 tickets; tickets 2 (5 days > 3), 4 (4 days > 3), 6 (8 days > 5) are SLA breaches; 5 are on time — 8 rows

hints: DATEDIFF('day', created_date, resolved_date) returns the number of calendar days between two dates.
Compare days_to_resolve against sla_days using CASE WHEN to label each ticket as 'SLA Breach' or 'On Time'.
explanation: DATEDIFF('day', start, end) computes elapsed days. Ticket 1: Sep 1→Sep 3 = 2 days ≤ 3 sla → On Time. Ticket 2: Sep 2→Sep 7 = 5 days > 3 → SLA Breach. Ticket 3: 1 day ≤ 2 → On Time. Ticket 4: 4 days > 3 → SLA Breach. Ticket 5: 1 day ≤ 2 → On Time. Ticket 6: 8 days > 5 → SLA Breach. Tickets 7 and 8: On Time. 3 breaches total.
